about: The facts tools/site_meta.py rests on, by the id its comments cite: what the site, the app's public pages or the position paper say, checked on 15 October 2026. source is a file in this repo or a public page; quote is its exact words (ignoring whitespace and HTML entities); visible_on lists the public addresses that show them. tools/check_site_meta.py checks that every id cited is here and that every quote from a page in this repo is still on it.

facts.claim: The product's full name is Stima Prova.
facts.quote: Stima Prova · The post-AI skill assessment

facts.claim: The short name Stima is used for the company and the product in the legal pages, the rubric page, the app and the position paper.
facts.quote: trading as Stima ("Stima", "we", "us"), operates the Stima Prova assessment platform at mystima.io.

facts.claim: Stima Prova is operated by Milkis Strategic Partners LLC, an Arizona limited liability company, trading as Stima.
facts.quote: Milkis Strategic Partners LLC, an Arizona limited liability company of 378 W Foothill St, Apache Junction, AZ 85120, trading as Stima

facts.claim: The footer of the main site pages names the product and the company as 'Stima Prova by Milkis Strategic Partners LLC'.
facts.quote: © 2026 Stima Prova by Milkis Strategic Partners LLC.

facts.claim: The position paper ties the name to its aim: an assessment should raise esteem, not just rank it, and 'Stima means both'.
facts.quote: Assessment should raise esteem, not just rank it. Stima means both.

facts.claim: A secondary line is 'AI-allowed assessment, with evidence.'
facts.quote: AI-allowed assessment, with evidence.

facts.claim: The footer describes the product as the post-AI skill assessment, AI-allowed by design, measured on a published scale, with every score cited to the record.
facts.quote: The post-AI skill assessment. AI-allowed by design, measured on a published scale, every score cited to the record.

facts.claim: The home page lists four principles: AI-allowed by design, evidence over detection, consent-first recording, humans confirm every outcome.
facts.quote: AI-allowed by design · Evidence over detection · Consent-first recording · Humans confirm every outcome

facts.claim: The legal documents describe Stima Prova as an assessment platform.
facts.quote: Stima Prova is an assessment platform run by Milkis Strategic Partners LLC

facts.claim: Stima Prova turns the assignment or take-home a team already uses into an AI-allowed session, grading the work on the customer's rubric and the AI use on a published scale, with every score cited to the record.
facts.quote: Stima Prova turns the assignment or take-home you already use into an AI-allowed session, grading the work on your rubric and the AI use on a published scale, every score cited to the record.

facts.claim: For hiring teams, Stima Prova offers AI-allowed take-homes with evidence.
facts.quote: For Hiring Teams AI-allowed take-homes, with evidence

facts.claim: For higher education, Stima Prova offers AI-allowed coursework, measured.
facts.quote: For Higher Education AI-allowed coursework, measured

facts.claim: For higher education, Stima Prova turns existing assignments into AI-allowed tasks that teach and measure responsible professional AI use.
facts.quote: Stima Prova turns the assignments you already teach into AI-allowed tasks that teach and measure responsible professional AI use.

facts.claim: The position paper is written for academic leaders, assessment designers, credentialing bodies and employers.
facts.quote: It is written for academic leaders, assessment designers, credentialing bodies, and employers

facts.claim: Step 1, Adapt: the customer brings one assignment or role question and Stima reshapes it with them, keeping the goals and rubric and adding a planted difficulty that a blind copy-paste gets wrong.
facts.quote: Bring one assignment or role question. We reshape it with you, same goals, same rubric, plus a planted difficulty a blind copy-paste gets wrong.

facts.claim: Step 2, Session: the person works one focused, timed session with AI explicitly allowed, recorded with consent, with no video recording and no lockdown browser.
facts.quote: The person works one focused, timed session with AI explicitly allowed, recorded with consent. No video recording. No lockdown browser.

facts.claim: Step 3, Two scores: the work is graded on the customer's rubric and the process on a published scale, and every score cites a moment in the session record.
facts.quote: The work, graded on your rubric. The process, graded on a published scale. Every score cites a moment in the session record.

facts.claim: Step 4, Confirm: a human confirms every outcome before it counts, and grades and decisions export as CSV for an LMS or ATS.
facts.quote: A human confirms every outcome before it counts. Grades and decisions export as CSV for your LMS or ATS, with a paper trail you can defend.

facts.claim: For hiring, step 1 is pasting the role description and the question already asked; Prova builds a real task from those words in minutes.
facts.quote: The role description and the question you already ask. Prova builds a real task from your own words, in minutes.

facts.claim: For hiring, step 4 delivers an explained report per candidate, risk flags beside the grade and a decision trail HR can defend.
facts.quote: An explained report per candidate, risk flags beside the grade, and a decision trail HR can defend.

facts.claim: For higher education, step 3 scores the work on the instructor's rubric and the AI use on the published Delegator, Operator, Director scale, each score citing the record.
facts.quote: Every score cites a moment in the record. The work on your rubric, the AI use on the published Delegator, Operator, Director scale.

facts.claim: For higher education, step 4 is the instructor confirming every outcome and exporting the grades for the LMS gradebook.
facts.quote: You confirm every outcome, then export the grades for your LMS gradebook.

facts.claim: The legal documents list Anthropic and OpenAI as the model vendors for participant workspace chat, with two capability tiers; Anthropic also generates results.
facts.quote: Anthropic Participant workspace chat (two capability tiers); generation of Results with structured output United States Prohibited under the contracted terms OpenAI Participant workspace chat (two capability tiers)

facts.claim: The quality of the work is a 0 to 100 score on the finished deliverable, graded blind on the customer's criteria with the rubric beside it.
facts.quote: A 0–100 score on the finished deliverable, graded blind on your criteria, with the rubric beside it.

facts.claim: The deliverable is graded blind on the customer's rubric, separately from the process.
facts.quote: The deliverable is graded blind on your rubric, separate from the process.

facts.claim: The AI collaboration level is Delegator, Operator or Director, read against what the task needed.
facts.quote: Delegator, Operator, or Director, read against what the task needed.

facts.claim: Each score points to a moment in the recorded session so the reasoning can be checked in one click.
facts.quote: Each score points to a moment in the recorded session. Check the reasoning in one click.

facts.claim: An AI model assigns the level and must cite sequence numbers from the evidence pack or excerpts from the work; a score without a valid citation is rejected.
facts.quote: An AI model assigns a level and must cite sequence numbers from the pack or excerpts from the work. A score without a valid citation is rejected.

facts.claim: The session is scored automatically by an AI model against Stima's rubric; the hiring decision and the grade are not automated.
facts.quote: Your session is scored by an AI model against our rubric. The score is produced automatically. The hiring decision and the grade are not.

facts.claim: By default the composite score is quality times 60% plus fit times 40% (right fit 100, one step off 50, two steps off 0), and the weights are shown to employers.
facts.quote: The composite score is quality × 60% + fit × 40% by default (right fit 100, one step off 50, two steps off 0). Weights are shown to employers and never hidden.

facts.claim: Risk flags sit beside the grade: unverified acceptance on high-stakes work and the blind pass are flagged even when the numbers look fine.
facts.quote: Unverified acceptance on high-stakes work and the blind pass get flagged, even when the numbers look fine.

facts.claim: The AI-collaboration scale has three levels: Delegator, Operator and Director.
facts.quote: Graded on the published Delegator, Operator, Director scale, read against what the task needed.

facts.claim: On the scale, higher is not better: what counts is whether the way of working fit what the task called for.
facts.quote: Higher is not better: what counts is whether the way of working fit what the task called for.

facts.claim: The home page headline for the scale is 'Three levels. Higher is not better.'
facts.quote: Three levels. Higher is not better.

facts.claim: The scale reads how much thinking was handed to the model (prompts, edits, verification, model switching, time), and the grade is calibration: the observed level against what the task demanded.
facts.quote: The scale reads how much thinking was handed to the model, prompts, edits, verification, model switching, time. The grade is calibration: the observed level against what the task demanded.

facts.claim: Level 1, Delegator (hands work to AI): restates the brief and accepts the first answer, which is right for verifiable, low-stakes work.
facts.quote: Restates the brief, accepts the first answer. Right for verifiable, low-stakes work.

facts.claim: Level 2, Operator (works with AI): iterates, corrects and edits substantively, the right default for mixed, everyday work.
facts.quote: Iterates, corrects, edits substantively. The right default for mixed, everyday work.

facts.claim: Level 3, Director (leads the work): sets the approach first, verifies the parts most likely wrong and owns the outcome.
facts.quote: Sets the approach first, verifies the parts most likely wrong, owns the outcome.

facts.claim: The published collaboration rubric is version collab-2.0.0.
facts.quote: export const RUBRIC_VERSION = "collab-2.0.0";

facts.claim: The rubric is published at mystima.io/rubric as 'Stima collaboration rubric · version collab-2.0.0'.
facts.quote: Stima collaboration rubric · version collab-2.0.0

facts.claim: The scale is the same for every employer and every task, so results compare across campaigns.
facts.quote: The scale is the same for every employer and every task, so results compare across campaigns.

facts.claim: The level is judged from the session record alone; the scorer is not told which way of working the task calls for, and the fit is computed afterwards.
facts.quote: The level is judged from the session record alone; the scorer is not told which way of working the task calls for. The fit is computed afterwards.

facts.claim: Recording is consent-first and workspace-only: no video recording, no keystroke logging and no lockdown browser, and participants see exactly what is kept before they start.
facts.quote: Workspace-only. No video recording, no keystroke logging, no lockdown browser. Participants see exactly what is kept before they start.

facts.claim: For hiring there is no video or audio recording and no keystroke logging, and candidates see exactly what is kept before they agree.
facts.quote: No video or audio recording, no keystroke logging. Candidates see exactly what is kept before they agree.

facts.claim: During the task the platform records the prompts sent, the model chosen, edits made afterwards, what is copied across, what is checked and how time is spent, plus IP address and basic browser and device information.
facts.quote: While you work, this platform records what you do: the prompts you send, which model you choose, the edits you make afterwards, what you copy across, what you check, and how your time is spent. It also records your IP address and basic browser and device information.

facts.claim: Nothing outside the assessment page is recorded: no camera, no microphone, no screen recording and no keystrokes outside the workspace.
facts.quote: We do not record anything you do outside this page. No camera, no microphone, no screen recording, no keystrokes outside this workspace.

facts.claim: While participants work, the platform records snapshots of their draft as they edit it and text they copy from a model response into their work.
facts.quote: snapshots of your draft as you edit it, and text you copy from a model response into your work

facts.claim: Stima does not infer participants' emotions.
facts.quote: We do not infer your emotions, and the platform is not built to.

facts.claim: Nothing is recorded about a session until the participant accepts the Participant Terms.
facts.quote: You accept these terms by selecting "I agree" below. Until you do, we record nothing about your session.

facts.claim: Stima Prova uses no proctoring and no prohibition of AI.
facts.quote: No proctoring. No prohibition. No black boxes.

facts.claim: The approach is AI-allowed by design: the question moves from whether people used AI to how well they used it.
facts.quote: Nothing to police, nothing to ban. The question moves from "did they use it" to "how well did they use it."

facts.claim: Every outcome is confirmed by a person; low-confidence results route to a reviewer, and participants can dispute.
facts.quote: Every outcome is confirmed by a person. Low-confidence results route to a reviewer, and participants can dispute.

facts.claim: Low-confidence results go to a human reviewer before anyone sees a rank; candidates can dispute, and disputes go to the same reviewer.
facts.quote: Low-confidence results go to a human reviewer before anyone sees a rank. Candidates can dispute; disputes go to the same reviewer.

facts.claim: Stima's contract with every customer requires meaningful human review, forbids using the report as the sole basis for an adverse decision and forbids automated rejection.
facts.quote: Our contract with every customer requires meaningful human review over any decision informed by your report, forbids using the report as the sole basis for an adverse decision, and forbids automated rejection.

facts.claim: A participant who thinks a report is wrong can email info@mystima.io with the reference on the result page, and Stima will look at the session.
facts.quote: If you think your report is wrong, email us at info@mystima.io with the reference on your result page. We will look at the session and tell you what we find.

facts.claim: In a course the report is not the grade: the instructor decides the grade and the institution's usual appeal route applies.
facts.quote: If this is a course, the report is not your grade. Your instructor decides your grade, and your institution's usual appeal route applies.

facts.claim: The home page summarises data handling as FERPA-aligned for campuses, hosted in the EU, DPA on request, no training on customer data, built to WCAG 2.1 AA.
facts.quote: FERPA-aligned for campuses, hosted in the EU, DPA on request, no training on your data. Built to WCAG 2.1 AA.

facts.claim: The platform runs in an EU region, and participant assessment data is stored there wherever the participant or customer is located.
facts.quote: We run the platform on infrastructure we control, in an EU region, hosted by the provider named in section 7. Participant assessment data is stored there regardless of where the participant or the customer is located.

facts.claim: Application and database hosting is provided by Scalaxy B.V. in the EU.
facts.quote: Scalaxy B.V. Application and database hosting EU

facts.claim: Model vendors, the email provider, the identity provider and research reviewers may process data outside the EEA.
facts.quote: Model vendors, the email provider, the identity provider and research reviewers may process data outside the EEA.

facts.claim: For campus IT review: hosted in the EU, nothing to install on the network, FERPA-aligned data handling, consent records, export and deletion on request, no training on student data, DPA on request, built to WCAG 2.1 AA.
facts.quote: Hosted in the EU, nothing to install on your network. FERPA-aligned data handling, consent records, export and deletion on request, no training on student data, DPA on request. Built to WCAG 2.1 AA.

facts.claim: Stima will not use assessment data, interaction records or results to train or fine-tune the weights of any AI model, its own or a third party's.
facts.quote: use Assessment Data, Interaction Records or Results to train, retrain or fine-tune the weights or parameters of any artificial intelligence model, whether Stima's own or a third party's;

facts.claim: The AI companies whose models participants use are contractually barred from using what participants send to train their models.
facts.quote: Those companies are contractually barred from using what you send to train their models.

facts.claim: Stima does use de-identified data to design and test its own rubrics, prompts and evaluation sets, which does not change any model.
facts.quote: We do use de-identified data to design and test our own rubrics, prompts and evaluation sets, which is a different operation and does not change any model.

facts.claim: Stima will not sell participant data.
facts.quote: We will not sell your data.

facts.claim: Participants must be 18 or over.
facts.quote: You must be 18 or over to take this assessment.

facts.claim: Assessment data, interaction records and results are kept for 12 months after a campaign or assignment closes, or 24 months with extended retention, then deleted.
facts.quote: Assessment Data, Interaction Records and Results for a campaign or assignment are retained for 12 months after the campaign or assignment closes, or 24 months where the order form provides for extended assessment retention, and are then deleted

facts.claim: The decision record (scoring runs, reviewer actions, disputes, disclosure versions and erasures) is exportable as structured data and retained for three years.
facts.quote: the decision record for any campaign or assignment, exportable as structured data, comprising every scoring run, reviewer action, dispute, disclosure version and erasure;

facts.claim: Data requests go to info@mystima.io and are answered within 30 days at no charge.
facts.quote: Write to info@mystima.io. We respond within 30 days. There is no charge, and we will not treat you differently for asking.

facts.claim: A participant's session, report and the evidence behind them are kept for 12 months after the campaign or assignment closes, or 24 months with extended retention; a legal hold placed by the customer suspends deletion.
facts.quote: Your session, report and the evidence behind it 12 months after the campaign or assignment closes, or 24 months where that customer has extended assessment retention. A legal hold placed by the customer suspends deletion.

facts.claim: The decision record (every scoring run, review action, dispute, disclosure version and erasure) is kept for three years.
facts.quote: The decision record: every scoring run, review action, dispute, disclosure version and erasure Three years.

facts.claim: Acceptance records, the answer to the research question and the wording versions shown are kept for as long as the session is retained and for 3 years after.
facts.quote: Your acceptance record, your answer to the research question, and the wording versions you saw For as long as the session is retained, and for 3 years thereafter

facts.claim: De-identified data derived from a session, and statistics published from it, are kept indefinitely; they are no longer personal data, so a deletion request does not reach them.
facts.quote: De-identified data derived from your session, and statistics published from it Indefinitely. It is no longer personal data and cannot be traced back to you, which also means a deletion request does not reach it.

facts.claim: A session record used in published research with the participant's consent is kept until the participant withdraws, or until an earlier date the institution agreed.
facts.quote: Your session record used in published research, where you said yes Until you withdraw, or until any earlier date your institution has agreed with us.

facts.claim: Stima creates de-identified data from assessment data and interaction records and uses it to operate, evaluate, secure, calibrate and improve the service, including validating scoring models, and for aggregate research.
facts.quote: Stima creates De-identified Data from Assessment Data and Interaction Records and uses it to operate, evaluate, secure, calibrate and improve the Service, including the validation of scoring models, and for Aggregate Research under clause 6.3(a).

facts.claim: Stima may publish aggregate findings and statistics from de-identified data; no customer, participant, role, course or organisation is identified and no individual session is published.
facts.quote: Stima may use De-identified Data, which is not personal data, for research and may publish aggregate findings and statistics derived from it. No Customer, Participant, role, course or organisation is identified, and no individual session is published.

facts.claim: Research on a session record that is not de-identified uses only the records of participants who gave explicit, separately recorded consent; the consent is optional and can be withdrawn.
facts.quote: Stima uses that record only in respect of Participants who have given explicit consent, separately recorded, through the consent screen at Schedule 1 Part 3. That consent is optional, is not a condition of taking or completing an assessment, has no bearing on Results or on any grade, is not disclosed to Customer, and may be withdrawn at any time.

facts.claim: In the education context, without a signed Research Annex, no research is done on student sessions and no de-identified data is created from them.
facts.quote: Neither Aggregate Research nor Session Research is performed on any session generated in the education context unless Customer has signed a Research Annex. Absent that Annex, Stima uses a Student's session solely to deliver the assessment to Customer, including the quality assurance of that Student's own Results described in clause 6.1, and to support and secure the Service. No De-identified Data is created from it

facts.claim: Three documents govern Stima Prova: the Terms of Use for customers, the Participant Terms for each participant and the Privacy Policy for everyone.
facts.quote: Three documents govern Stima Prova. The Terms of Use bind the organisation that runs assessments, the Participant Terms bind each person who takes one, and the Privacy Policy explains what happens to data for everyone.

facts.claim: Grades and decisions export as CSV for an LMS or ATS.
facts.quote: Grades and decisions export as CSV for your LMS or ATS, with a paper trail you can defend.

facts.claim: Canvas LTI 1.3 with grade passback is coming; it is not available yet.
facts.quote: Confirmed grades export for your LMS. Canvas LTI 1.3 with grade passback is coming.

facts.claim: On the Enterprise plan, white label, SSO and integrations are add-ons.
facts.quote: White label, SSO and integrations as add-ons.

facts.claim: Decision-record export is included on every hiring plan.
facts.quote: Decision-record export

facts.claim: Self-serve plans are paid by card through Stripe and can be cancelled from the billing page.
facts.quote: Self-serve plans are paid by card through Stripe and can be cancelled from your billing page.

facts.claim: Hiring sessions run up to 90 minutes.
facts.quote: Sessions up to 90 minutes

facts.claim: The session time limit is set by the organisation, and the timer keeps running if an AI provider is unavailable.
facts.quote: Your time limit keeps running, because the timer is set by the organisation and we do not stop it automatically.

facts.claim: A completed assessment is a submitted piece of work, including work submitted automatically when time runs out; invites, opens and drop-offs cost nothing.
facts.quote: A candidate submitted their work, including work submitted automatically when time runs out. Invites, opens and drop-offs cost nothing.

facts.claim: The hiring free trial covers one role and 10 completions for 14 days, with a card on file; cancelling before the trial ends means nothing is charged.
facts.quote: One role, 10 completions, 14 days. Card on file; cancel before the trial ends and nothing is charged.

facts.claim: The sign-up page offers 14 days free with 1 role and 10 completed assessments; a card is added after sign-in and charged only when the trial ends.
facts.quote: 14 days free: 1 role and 10 completed assessments. After you sign in you add a card; it is charged only when the trial ends, and you can cancel before.

facts.claim: Hiring plans charge $29 per completed assessment on every plan; invites, opens and drop-outs cost nothing.
facts.quote: $29 per completed assessment on every plan. Invites, opens and candidates who drop out cost nothing.

facts.claim: Pay as you go costs $29 per completed assessment, with no minimum, no credits and no lock-in.
facts.quote: Pay as you go $29 each Per completed assessment. No minimum, no credits, no lock-in.

facts.claim: Team costs $299 a month with 10 completions a month included, then $29 each, with reviewer roles and a decision trail, or $2,990 a year.
facts.quote: Team $299 / mo 10 completions a month included, then $29 each. Reviewer roles, decision trail. Or $2,990 a year.

facts.claim: Comply costs $690 a month with 25 completions included, DPA on request, org structure and extended data storage, or $6,900 a year.
facts.quote: Comply $690 / mo 25 completions included. DPA on request, org structure, extended data storage. Or $6,900 a year.

facts.claim: Enterprise starts from $15K a year on an annual contract with committed volume.
facts.quote: Enterprise From $15K / yr Annual contract plus committed volume.

facts.claim: Annual billing on Team and Comply gives two months free.
facts.quote: Annual billing on Team and Comply: two months free.

facts.claim: Instructors use Stima Prova free: one course, up to 250 student sessions per term, no card and no IT ticket.
facts.quote: One course, up to 250 student sessions per term. No card, no IT ticket.

facts.claim: The Department plan costs $12K a year for up to 1,500 enrollments a year, about $8 per student per course.
facts.quote: Department $12K / yr Up to 1,500 enrollments a year. Works out to $8 per student per course.

facts.claim: The College plan costs $35K a year for up to 5,000 enrollments a year, about $7 per student per course.
facts.quote: College $35K / yr Up to 5,000 enrollments a year. Works out to $7 per student per course.

facts.claim: The Institution plan costs $90K a year for up to 15,000 enrollments a year, about $6 per student per course.
facts.quote: Institution $90K / yr Up to 15,000 enrollments a year. Works out to $6 per student per course.

facts.claim: An enrollment is one student in one course; campus plans are billed annually and paid upfront, usage above the tier moves the campus up at renewal, and larger systems are priced by quote.
facts.quote: An enrollment is one student in one course. Annual billing, paid upfront. Usage above your tier moves you up at renewal. Larger systems priced by quote.

facts.claim: Campus plans are priced per student, not per seat.
facts.quote: Priced per student, not per seat.

facts.claim: Candidates are always free, with one practice session every 90 days.
facts.quote: Candidates always free, one practice session every 90 days.

facts.claim: Candidates get a shorter, AI-allowed process with a verified result they own and can share.
facts.quote: Shorter, AI-allowed, with a verified result they own and can share.

facts.claim: Each assignment produces a verifiable credential (Open Badges 3.0) and a shareable result page, dated and explained.
facts.quote: Each assignment produces a verifiable credential (Open Badges 3.0) and a shareable result page, dated and explained.

facts.claim: Stima's position paper is 'Assessment After AI', Position Paper No. 01.
facts.quote: Stima Prova · Position Paper No. 01 · Free

facts.quote: PDF · 9 pages 5 references Free with your email

facts.quote: Position Paper No. 01 · PDF · 9 pages

facts.claim: The paper argues why banning AI from assessment tests a world that no longer exists, what to measure instead, and how a credential survives when any answer can be generated.
facts.quote: Why banning AI from assessment tests a world that no longer exists, what to measure instead, and how a credential survives when any answer can be generated.

facts.claim: The paper is a 2026 pre-launch edition.
facts.quote: POSITION PAPER · NO. 01 2026 · PRE-LAUNCH EDITION

facts.quote: placeholder="Tell us about your course, your open role, or your team... *"

facts.quote: General: info@mystima.io
